meta.tagline: You never log a transaction; you only set the rules.
meta.description: PeraPlano is a Philippines-first Android app that tracks your money automatically by reading the notifications your banks and e-wallets already send you — on your phone, never on a server.

footer.promise: Local-first · No ads · Your data is never sold

serviceStatus.heading: What PeraPlano runs today
paragraphs: PeraPlano is an Android app. It has no sign-in, no user accounts, and no multi-device sync.
Everything the app records lives in an encrypted database on your own phone. There is no copy on our servers to look at, to hand over, or to delete.
Cloud backup and multi-device sync are described in our planning documents as future PeraPlano Plus features. They are not available, and no part of your ledger is transmitted anywhere today.

One exception, and it is not your ledger: if you signed up as a beta tester, we hold the email address you gave us so Google Play can invite you to the closed test. That list is described in full in the privacy notice, and asking to be removed takes one message.

counselRequired.heading: Clauses a lawyer still has to write
counselRequired.intro: Five clauses on this page were drafted in-house and are published above, each stamped as a draft, so you can at least read what we intend to be bound by. Two were not drafted, and neither is a writing problem — each is blocked on a decision that does not exist yet:
clauses: Governing law and venue — blocked on the company. There is no registered entity behind PeraPlano yet, so there is no domicile to name and no seat to sue in. Naming a court before the company that would answer in it exists is guesswork dressed up as a clause.

Subscription term, renewal, cancellation and refund terms — blocked on Google Play's subscription policies, which set much of what these terms are even allowed to say, and on a price that has not been decided. There is nothing to renew and nothing to refund yet.
counselRequired.consequence: PeraPlano Plus cannot be offered for sale until these exist. The five drafted above are also waiting on counsel; the difference is that those can be read today and these two cannot yet be written.

unfilledRoles.heading: Three roles behind this app are unfilled
paragraphs: PeraPlano is built by one person, and three things Philippine data-protection practice expects of an organisation handling personal data do not exist yet. There is no registered company acting as the Personal Information Controller. There is no appointed Data Protection Officer. There is no registration with the National Privacy Commission.

You are reading that here rather than finding it out later. Everywhere on this site where one of those identifiers belongs, the page prints a marker saying the value is required and missing, and a deployment that tried to publish a plausible-looking placeholder instead would refuse to start. An invented controller name or a made-up officer is worse than an admitted gap, because it reads as compliance to everyone who does not check.

This is survivable today for one reason: the app keeps your ledger on your phone and sends none of it anywhere, so there is no company-held copy of anyone's financial data for a controller to be responsible for. It stops being survivable the day cloud backup ships — which is why PeraPlano Plus is not offered for sale until all three exist.
unfilledRoles.invitation: If you are a Philippine privacy practitioner, a Data Protection Officer, or a lawyer who works on RA 10173, and this is the kind of gap you would rather help close than read about, write to the support address below.

howItWorks.heading: How it works
howItWorks.lede: Five steps. You are involved in exactly one of them.

beats.line: You are told what will be read, before any system screen appears.
beats.long: Before any system screen appears, the app tells you what Notification Access is for, what it will read, and what it discards. Every permission is skippable; skip it and the app falls back to manual entry rather than refusing to work.

beats.line: Recognised notifications are read on the device, never uploaded.
beats.long: The listener runs continuously. Each notification from a provider it recognises is read on the device — never uploaded — and turned into a structured record: amount, direction, merchant, wallet, category, confidence.

beats.line: Confident readings post themselves. The rest wait for one tap.
beats.long: High-confidence readings are recorded automatically. Anything the app is unsure about waits in the Review Queue for a one-tap confirmation, and every correction you make becomes a rule that replays on future notifications.

beats.line: Duplicates collapse, and moving your own money is not spending.
beats.long: A push and an SMS announcing the same payment are collapsed into one record. Moving money between your own wallets is detected as a transfer and excluded from both spending and income, so your own money does not look like expenditure.

beats.line: Limits, goals and bills update the moment a transaction commits.
beats.long: Committed transactions update your limits, goals, bills and your Safe-to-Spend number in real time. The app notifies you when something you set a rule about happens, and stays quiet otherwise.

whoItIsFor.heading: Who it is for
whoItIsFor.lede: Three people, one app, no mode switches. Most readers are more than one of them.

personas.name: The salaried kinsenas earner
personas.definition: kinsenas — paid twice a month, on the 15th and 30th, the second one also called katapusan
personas.pain: The second week of each half-month, when the money runs thin and nothing explains where it went.
personas.gives: Limits that reset on your real payday, not on the 1st.
personas.long: Salary lands in a payroll bank account, part of it moves to GCash for daily spending, and rent, bills and padala cluster right after payday. PeraPlano gives you an income cadence tuned to a twice-monthly pay cycle, limits that reset on your real payday rather than on the first of the month, and a Safe-to-Spend number that understands how many days are left until the 15th.

personas.name: The gig or informal-income worker
personas.definition: utang — money owed, tracked in both directions, to you and by you
personas.pain: No payroll summary exists. Your notification history is your income record.
personas.gives: Every incoming payment captured, and the week totalled honestly.
personas.long: Driver, freelancer, online seller, service provider. Income arrives irregularly through GCash, Maya or bank transfers, sometimes several small payments in a day. PeraPlano gives you automatic capture of every incoming payment, an irregular income cadence you can override, in-versus-out reporting that says whether a week actually netted positive, and loan tracking for the informal credit that bridges slow weeks.

personas.name: The e-wallet-heavy spender
personas.definition: padala — money sent home to family, a default category rather than an afterthought
personas.pain: Internal transfers make every app double-count, and no single place shows the whole picture.
personas.gives: Your own transfers detected, so they never read as spending.
personas.long: Often the designated money person in the family. Daily life runs through GCash and Maya — load, transport, food delivery, online shopping, bills, padala to the province — across three or more apps at once. PeraPlano models multiple wallets properly, detects transfers automatically so a GCash-to-bank move is never counted as spending, and surfaces the quiet recurring subscriptions you forgot about.

whyThePhilippines.heading: Why the Philippines
whyThePhilippines.lede: Six facts about Filipino money. No global competitor is built around all six at once.

facts.line: are default rails for tens of millions.
facts.long: E-wallet saturation. GCash and Maya are default payment rails for tens of millions of people. QR payments, send-money and buy-load are daily events, and every one of them emits a notification that can be read.

facts.line: for every debit and credit, without SMS permission.
facts.long: Notification-rich banking. Philippine banks and digital banks send push or SMS alerts for debits and credits. Even a bank SMS surfaces as a notification from your default messaging app, which the listener can read without ever requesting SMS permission.

facts.line: is the rhythm, and monthly budgeting never fits it.
facts.long: A distinct pay rhythm. Salaried workers are paid kinsenas — twice a month, on the 15th and 30th. Budgeting apps built for monthly cycles never fit; PeraPlano treats the twice-monthly cadence as first-class.

facts.line: is everywhere, and it runs in both directions.
facts.long: A distinct debt culture. Informal borrowing is everywhere: utang between friends and family, 5-6 lending, appliance instalments, salary loans, credit cards. PeraPlano tracks loans in both directions.

facts.line: is a budget line, not an edge case.
facts.long: Remittance flows. Padala is routine and budgeted, not an edge case, so it is a category the app ships with.

facts.line: is the market, and the only place listening is possible.
facts.long: Android dominance. The market is overwhelmingly Android, which is also the only platform where notification listening is possible at all. Android-only is a fit, not a compromise.

privacyPromise.heading: Nothing leaves your phone
privacyPromise.lede: This is architecture, not a policy promise.
points: Notifications are read and parsed on the device.
No account, no sign-in, no server copy of your ledger.
Raw notification text is encrypted, kept 30 days, then purged.
paragraphs: Raw notification text never leaves your phone. It is stored encrypted on the device with a 30-day time-to-live so you can always answer the question why did the app record this, and then it is purged.
This is architecture, not a policy promise. There is no account, no sign-in and no server copy of your ledger, so there is nothing on our side to hand over, to lose, or to be asked for.
Cloud backup of committed transaction records — structured fields, never raw text — is a planned paid feature and is opt-in. It does not exist yet.

whatItIsNot.heading: What it is not
whatItIsNot.intro: A money app that oversells itself is a money app you should not trust.
bullets: Not a bank or an e-money issuer. PeraPlano never holds, moves or touches your funds. It observes and it plans.
Not a financial advisor. It reports facts against rules you set. It does not recommend products, investments or credit.
No ads and no data selling, ever. The intended business model is a subscription.
No SMS permission, ever. Bank SMS is read as a notification from your messaging app, so the permission is neither requested nor needed.
Not a bookkeeping tool. No invoicing, VAT, payroll or BIR features — gig workers are served as people managing personal cash flow, not as businesses.

support.title: Support
support.intro: This page is two things: how to reach a person, and the complete list of what you can switch off, correct, export or destroy without reaching anyone at all. The second list is longer, and for most questions it is the faster answer.

howToReachUs.heading: How to reach us
paragraphs: Support is by email. There is no in-app chat and no phone line, and we would rather say so than leave you looking for one.

The company operating PeraPlano is the Personal Information Controller for any personal data it actually receives — which, today, means support correspondence and content-free diagnostics, and nothing from your ledger.

beforeYouWrite.heading: Before you write to us
paragraphs: Please do not paste raw notification text into a support message. The text your bank or e-wallet sends you is the most sensitive thing the app handles: on your phone it is encrypted and purged after 30 days, and it is never transmitted anywhere. Pasted into an email it becomes an ordinary message in an ordinary mailbox, and none of that protection follows it.
Describe the problem instead — which provider, roughly when, and what the app got wrong. That is almost always enough, and where it is not we will ask for the smallest thing that is.
Support correspondence is kept for no longer than 24 months after your case is closed, and sooner if you ask for it to be deleted.

unshipped.heading: Two rows in the tables below describe something that has not shipped
unshipped.body: Cloud backup, and the sign-in identity that exists only to carry it, are planned PeraPlano Plus features. They are listed because this is the complete list of controls the product commits to, not the list of controls that are live today. Nothing of yours is on a server, so there is currently nothing for those two controls to act on.

rights.heading: Your rights under RA 10173, and how to use them
rights.intro: The Data Privacy Act of 2012 gives you these rights. Each one maps to a control that already exists in the app rather than to a request form, because a right you have to ask us to honour is slower than a right you can exercise yourself.
rights.caption: Each right under the Data Privacy Act of 2012, and the control that delivers it.
rows: A layered privacy notice, plus short in-flow explainers shown at the moment of each permission ask.
Every permission is skippable; ingest can be paused globally or per provider; telemetry can be switched off; consent can be withdrawn at any time.
Transparency screens show exactly why the app recorded a transaction, for as long as the notification text is retained, plus a full data export.
Every parsed field is editable, Review Queue corrections apply immediately, and those corrections become rules that replay going forward.
Delete any single transaction; wipe everything on the device and, where backup was enabled, the server copies; turning backup off deletes server copies.
Export everything: a CSV of the ledger plus a full structured export of wallets, limits, goals, loans, bills, recurring patterns, rules and your income profile.
Right to damages, or to complain
The Data Protection Officer's contact and the complaint route to the National Privacy Commission are both stated below.

dpo.heading: Data Protection Officer
paragraphs: A Data Protection Officer is appointed before public launch regardless of whether registration thresholds are met. Write to the officer directly about anything on this page, or about a right you want to exercise that the app does not already hand you.

Registration with the National Privacy Commission is our planning position rather than a settled conclusion — which obligations attach, given that the free tier keeps everything on your own phone, is still with Philippine privacy counsel. The status as it stands today is printed below.

complaints.heading: Complaining to the National Privacy Commission
paragraphs: If you are not satisfied with how we handled your data or your request, you can complain to the National Privacy Commission, the Philippine regulator for the Data Privacy Act of 2012.

We are not printing an address, a phone number or a link for the Commission here. Contact details for a regulator change, and a stale one on a page like this sends someone somewhere that no longer answers. Look the Commission up directly. If you tell us you intend to complain, that is not a reason for us to close your case.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: PeraPlano is local-first by architecture, not by policy promise: the notification text your banks and e-wallets already send you is read on your own phone, stored encrypted on that phone with a 30-day time-to-live, and never leaves it under any configuration. The only thing designed to sync off the device is committed transaction records — structured fields, never raw text — and only if you explicitly switch on cloud backup, a PeraPlano Plus feature. Syncing is not the only way data can leave a phone, so the table below lists every category that does: content-free diagnostics you can switch off, any export file you create yourself, and anything you choose to put in a support message. There are no ads, no data selling, and no third-party analytics that receive notification content.
privacy.sourceHeading: Where this notice comes from, and what it still lacks
privacy.sourceNote: This notice is derived from PeraPlano's internal privacy and compliance document, which is marked {status}. That document has not been reviewed by Philippine privacy counsel, so neither has this page.

whoIsResponsible.heading: Who is responsible
paragraphs: The company operating PeraPlano is the Personal Information Controller under the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act 10173) for any personal data it actually receives and controls: cloud backup contents, the sign-in identity used for backup, support correspondence, and aggregate telemetry.

Any infrastructure vendor that stores encrypted backups on the company's behalf acts as a Personal Information Processor. A written outsourcing agreement covering confidentiality, security measures, sub-processing and breach assistance is required before cloud backup ships.

Data processed entirely on your own device, for your own household finances, arguably falls under the Act's personal and household exemption as far as your own processing is concerned. PeraPlano does not rely on that argument. The app is designed, documented and reviewed as if every piece of data it touches were fully in scope, because that keeps the compliance story simple and truthful.

A Data Protection Officer is appointed before public launch regardless of whether registration thresholds are met. Registering that appointment with the National Privacy Commission, together with the backup data processing system, is our planning position rather than a settled conclusion: which registration obligations actually attach, given that the free tier keeps everything on your own phone, is still with Philippine privacy counsel. Where registration is required it happens before cloud backup goes live, and no later than public launch. The status as it stands today is printed below.

whyWeProcess.caption: The purpose and the lawful basis for each thing PeraPlano does with your data.

Consent, recorded in the app before you grant Notification Access

The consent is specific to one purpose — automatically recording money movements from your notifications. It is freely given: every permission is skippable and the app degrades to manual entry. It is withdrawable: you can pause listening, revoke access, or wipe everything.
Cloud backup and multi-device sync (PeraPlano Plus)

Consent, or necessity for a contract

The app's own alerts: limit thresholds, bill reminders, loan reminders, goal updates, the daily Review Queue digest, listener health, and the payday summary
Necessity for the service you configured
Delivered on your device. On Android 13 and later this needs the notification-posting permission; declining it blocks nothing, because every alert also appears inside the app.

whatDataExists.invariantsHeading: Three rules that bind the table above
invariants: Raw notification text never syncs, and is purged after 30 days.

Every automatically recorded transaction keeps a reference to the notification it came from for as long as that raw text is retained, so you can always answer "why did the app record this?" After the 30-day purge the structured record remains and the raw text view says the original notification is no longer retained.
Wipe means wipe: on-device stores and, where backup was enabled, server copies.

howProcessingHappens.heading: How processing happens
paragraphs: Processing happens on your phone. Your bank or e-wallet posts a notification, the listener receives it, the parser reads structured fields out of the text, and the result is written to an encrypted database on the device. The raw text is kept only so the app can show you why it recorded something and re-read it if a parser improves — and only for 30 days.
The minimization stance behind that design:
bullets: Extract, then discard. Only structured fields are kept: amount, direction, merchant, reference number, the balance after the transaction where the notification gives one, and the timestamp.

The unknown-notification bin is not a dragnet. Notifications from apps PeraPlano does not recognize are captured only so you can flag "this is a money notification" in the Review Queue, and they follow the same on-device-only, 30-day-purge rule as raw notification text.
Telemetry counts, never content. A parser failure report carries the provider's identity and a failure class, never the text that failed to parse.
No enrichment. PeraPlano does not look up, buy, or infer additional data about you or the people you transact with from any outside source.

Collection follows function. Every field in the data model exists because a shipped feature reads it; nothing is collected speculatively. Adding a field to anything that syncs requires an update to the table above, a review of the Play Data safety declaration, and a check of this notice in the same release.

betaProgramme.heading: The beta tester list
paragraphs: If you signed up on the beta page, we hold the Google account email you gave us, a first name, an optional phone model, the date you submitted it, and the fact that you ticked the consent box. Nothing else.

The basis is your consent and the purpose is single: adding you to the closed test in Google Play Console so that Google can send you the invitation. Google acts as our processor for the spreadsheet the list lives in, and as the distributor of the test itself.

It is kept until public release plus ninety days, or until you ask to be removed, whichever comes first. Removal is by request to the support mailbox named in this notice, and the data deletion page describes the route.
This is the only category of personal data PeraPlano keeps on a server. Your ledger is not part of it, is not linked to it, and still never leaves your phone.

whoReceivesIt.heading: Who receives your data
paragraphs: Nobody today. There is one designed exception and it has not shipped: when cloud backup is released, the infrastructure vendor holding those encrypted backups on the company's behalf will act as a Personal Information Processor, and a written outsourcing agreement covering confidentiality, security measures, sub-processing and breach assistance has to be in place before that release. No such vendor holds anything of yours now, and no other party receives your ledger.
There is no advertising, no data selling, and no third-party advertising or marketing recipient of any kind.
Two things reach the company rather than a third party: content-free aggregate telemetry, which you can switch off without losing a feature, and any support message you choose to send.
Purchase processing for PeraPlano Plus is handled by Google Play under its own policies. PeraPlano stores no payment instrument data.

automatedDecisions.heading: Automated decisions, and how to correct them
paragraphs: PeraPlano processes your data automatically. It parses notifications into structured transactions, assigns categories, detects recurring payments, removes duplicates, and links transfers between your own wallets.

Every one of those decisions is correctable by you. Low-confidence parses go to the Review Queue for you to confirm or fix, every parsed field — amount, direction, wallet, category, merchant, note — is editable, and your corrections become rules that replay going forward.

You can also see why a decision was made. For any automatically recorded transaction, the transparency screen shows the parsed fields side by side with the notification text they came from, for as long as that text is retained.

yourRights.heading: Your rights
yourRights.caption: Your rights under the Data Privacy Act of 2012, and the control in the app that delivers each one.
rows: This notice, plus short plain-language explainers shown in the app at the moment of each permission ask.
Every permission is skippable. Reading can be paused globally or for one provider, telemetry can be switched off, and consent can be withdrawn at any time.

Transparency screens: each automatically recorded transaction keeps a reference to the notification it came from while that text is retained, so you can see exactly why the app recorded it. You can also export everything.
Every parsed field is editable, the Review Queue lets you correct low-confidence parses, and corrections become rules that replay going forward.
Delete any single transaction, or wipe everything — on-device data and, where backup was enabled, server copies. Switching backup off deletes the server copies.
Export everything: a CSV of the ledger plus a full structured export of your wallets, limits, goals, loans, bills, recurring patterns, rules and income profile.
The Data Protection Officer's contact is at the top of this notice, and the complaint route to the National Privacy Commission is below.

complaints.heading: Complaints
paragraphs: Write to the Data Protection Officer first, at the address at the top of this notice. Most things are fixed faster that way.
You also have the right to complain to the National Privacy Commission, the Philippine authority for the Data Privacy Act of 2012, and you can do that independently of anything PeraPlano does.

This page deliberately does not print an address, phone number or web link for the Commission. PeraPlano's own documents record no verified contact detail for it, and publishing one we have not verified would be worse than publishing none. Use the Commission's own published channels.

notRequested.heading: What we deliberately do not ask for
notRequested.caption: Permissions and data sources PeraPlano does not request, and why.
rows: Google Play's SMS and Call Log policy effectively prohibits reading SMS for expense tracking. Bank SMS still reach PeraPlano as notifications posted by your default SMS app, which the listener reads like any other notification.
Accessibility services as a way in
Explicitly ruled out. Using accessibility APIs to collect data violates Play policy and would poison the trust story this product is built on.
No product use. Counterparty names come only from the notification text your providers already sent you.

otherPeoplesNames.heading: Other people's names in your notifications
paragraphs: Notifications can carry personal data about people who do not use PeraPlano and never agreed to anything — most often the name of whoever sent you money (a padala, or remittance) or the other party to a loan. That is worth addressing directly rather than leaving unsaid.
PeraPlano's stance:
bullets: Context of origin. Those names were already delivered to your own device by your own provider; PeraPlano introduces no new disclosure. Your record of who paid you is ordinary household record-keeping.

Minimize anyway. Only the short counterparty label needed for the merchant field, for category matching and for matching loan payments is kept in structured form. Everything else in the raw text disappears with the 30-day purge.

On-device by default. Third-party names sit on your device. They would reach company infrastructure only inside an encrypted backup of your own ledger, where the company acts as controller of your data — not as a collector of theirs.
You can edit them. Counterparty and merchant labels can be changed or removed at any time, and a rule can rename them permanently.
Never used beyond your ledger. Third-party names are never aggregated across users, never used to match one user to another, and never included in telemetry.

ifSomethingGoesWrong.heading: If something goes wrong
paragraphs: A company breach means a compromise of systems the company controls: backup storage, the telemetry pipeline, the sign-in identity store. Losing your phone, or having it stolen, is not a company breach — that is what on-device encryption and your device lock are for — but the wipe control and recovery guidance are documented in our support materials.

The Act's list of sensitive personal information does not name financial transaction data. PeraPlano treats your whole ledger, and everything derived from your notifications, at that higher protection level anyway: notification text can incidentally contain things that are on the list, such as fragments of a government ID number in a verification message, and loan records reveal indebtedness.

So where a breach involves that data and there is a real risk of serious harm, the company notifies the National Privacy Commission and the people affected within 72 hours of knowing, or having reason to believe, that a breach occurred.

Our internal document commits to the preparation shipping with the product rather than after it: a breach response runbook covering detection, containment, assessment, notification and remediation; pre-drafted notification templates for users and for the Commission; a breach log kept even for incidents that do not require notification; and an annual rehearsal. That is the standard we hold ourselves to and it is written down, but none of it has been built yet, and we would rather say so than let this page imply a readiness we have not reached.

The architecture limits the damage. Backups are encrypted, and raw notification text is never on any server, so the worst case on the server side exposes structured records — never the text of your notifications.

terms.title: Terms
terms.draftMark: DRAFT — drafted in-house and not yet reviewed by Philippine counsel. It is published rather than withheld so you can read what we intend to be bound by, and it may change.
terms.intro: This page states what PeraPlano is and is not, what the free and paid tiers contain, and what a lawyer still has to write before anything here can be sold. The last part is on the page rather than in a backlog, because a terms document with an invisible hole in it is one nobody ever fills.

whatPeraPlanoIs.heading: What PeraPlano is, in contractual terms
paragraphs: PeraPlano is an app that observes and plans. It never holds, moves, or touches funds. It is not a bank, an e-money issuer, a payment service, or any kind of regulated financial institution, and it never becomes one — this is a permanent product commitment, not a description of the current release.
PeraPlano is not a financial advisor. It reports facts against rules you set yourself. It does not recommend products, investments or credit, and nothing it shows you is advice.
There are no ads and no data selling, ever. The intended business model is a subscription, and monetising your attention or your data would destroy the one thing this product depends on.

theLedgerIsDerived.heading: Your ledger is derived, and checking it is on you
paragraphs: PeraPlano builds your ledger by reading notifications your banks and e-wallets already send you, and by interpreting text those providers can change without telling anyone. High-confidence readings are recorded automatically; low-confidence ones wait in the Review Queue for you to confirm or correct.

That means a parse can be wrong. An amount can be misread, a transfer can be counted twice, a provider can change a message format overnight and break a rule that worked yesterday. Every recorded transaction shows you the notification it came from, and every field is editable, precisely because you are the one who has to be able to check it.
PeraPlano is not a substitute for your bank's or e-wallet's own records. Where the app and your provider disagree, your provider is right.

What follows from that legally — how liability for an inaccurate parse is limited, and what warranty is or is not given — is a lawyer question and has not been drafted. It is listed at the bottom of this page with the rest of what is missing.

tiers.heading: Free and Plus
tiers.intro: Automatic tracking is never limited by tier. The free tier is meant to stay genuinely useful forever; paying buys depth — more wallets, unlimited limits and goals, full loan amortisation, longer history, projection and backup.
tiers.caption: The locked capability matrix for the free and Plus tiers.
afterTable: The matrix above is the locked definition of the tiers, and it describes the intended shape of the product on the day PeraPlano Plus becomes purchasable — not the app you can install right now. No one is on a limited tier today: tier limits are not enforced at all in the current build, every capability is built and working, and everyone using the app has full capability whatever the Free column says. The entitlement layer that applies these caps is switched on later, in one place; when it is, the caps apply going forward and never retroactively.

When that happens, hitting a cap will block creation, never destruction. A free user over a cap — more than 90 days of history, say — keeps the data beyond it: it is hidden, not deleted, and restoring Plus restores visibility. Existing data is never deleted and never retroactively hidden because of a tier.

Privacy controls are never Plus-gated. Pausing, wiping, the transparency screens, telemetry opt-out and the full data export are available on every tier, because a right is not a feature. The Export row in the matrix above refers only to the Plus convenience export in Reports; exporting everything you own is ungated and always will be.

One privacy consequence of the matrix is worth stating plainly: because cloud backup is a Plus capability, the app never transmits a free-tier user's financial data off the device at all. Today it transmits nobody's — cloud backup has not shipped in any tier.

betaTesters.heading: Beta testers keep Plus
paragraphs: If you joined the closed test through the beta page and took part in it, you keep PeraPlano Plus at no cost after public release, for as long as the app is published and Plus exists as a tier. It is not a trial, a discount, or a first year free.
The record is the signup list itself: the address you gave us and the date you gave it. If you are on that list and Plus is ever charged for, you are not charged.

Two boundaries, stated rather than discovered later. If PeraPlano is discontinued there is nothing left to grant, so this ends with the app. And if the tiers are ever renamed or reorganised, you keep the equivalent of what Plus covered on the day you joined, not whatever a future tier happens to be called.

pricingNotPublished.heading: Pricing is not published yet
paragraphs: No price for PeraPlano Plus has been decided, so none is published here. Nothing on this site is an offer to sell you anything, and there is currently no way to buy Plus at any price.

Prices, the billing period, and the renewal, cancellation and refund terms will appear on this page before any purchase is possible. If you are reading this and cannot find a price, that is not an omission — it is the current state of the product.

purchases.heading: Purchases, when they exist, run through Google Play
paragraphs: When PeraPlano Plus becomes purchasable it will be sold through Google Play, and purchase state will be managed by Google Play under its own policies and its own terms with you. Your subscription, its renewal and any refund are handled there.

PeraPlano stores no payment instrument data. No card number, no bank account, no wallet credential ever reaches the app or the company; what the app keeps is a local flag saying which tier you are on.

intellectualProperty.heading: Intellectual property, and the licence you get when you install
paragraphs: PeraPlano belongs to the company that operates it — the app, its source code, the parsers and provider rules that read your notifications, the designs, this text, and the PeraPlano name and logo. Installing the app transfers none of that to you.

What you get is a licence: a personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable and revocable right to install and use PeraPlano on devices you control, for your own household finances. You may not sell, rent, sublicense or redistribute the app, and you may not reverse-engineer, decompile or disassemble it — except to the extent Philippine law permits you to regardless of what this paragraph says.

The reverse of that matters more, and it is not a courtesy. Your ledger is yours. Every transaction, wallet, limit, goal, loan and rule you create — and everything the app derives on your behalf — belongs to you, not to us. This licence gives the company no ownership of your financial data and no right to use it. The ungated export control exists so that is something you can act on rather than something you have to take our word for.
The PeraPlano name and logo are reserved. Using the app does not give you any right to use them.

terminationAndSuspension.heading: Termination and suspension
paragraphs: This clause is unusually short, and the reason is architectural rather than generous: PeraPlano has no account, no sign-in and no server-side identity. There is nothing of yours that we hold, and therefore nothing of yours that we could suspend.

You end this agreement by uninstalling the app, or by wiping its data from inside it. No notice to us is required, because there is nothing on our side that knows you were ever here. Nothing has to be closed, cancelled or requested.

We can stop distributing the app, stop publishing updates, or withdraw it from Google Play. That ends what we owe you going forward; it does not reach into your phone. A copy already installed keeps working on the data already on your device until you remove it.

If a sign-in identity is ever introduced — it would arrive with cloud backup, which is a Plus capability that has not shipped — then suspending that identity becomes possible for the first time, and this clause is revised in the same release, alongside the account-deletion route Google Play requires. Until that day, the paragraphs above are the whole of it.

limitationOfLiability.heading: Limitation of liability, and what is not warranted
paragraphs: PeraPlano is provided as it is. We do not warrant that it is free of defects, that it will run uninterrupted on your device, or — the one that matters — that any particular reading of a notification is correct.

The failure modes are named two sections above, and they are real rather than theoretical: an amount can be misread, a transfer can be counted twice, a provider can change its message format overnight and break a rule that worked yesterday, and a notification that never arrives is a transaction the app never sees. The product is built to make each of those visible and correctable — every record shows the notification it came from, every field is editable, low-confidence readings wait in the Review Queue — and none of that makes it a system of record.

So: your bank's and your e-wallet's own statements are the record. PeraPlano is not a substitute for them, and checking any figure you are about to act on is your responsibility. We do not accept liability for a decision taken on a number the app derived, for money moved or not moved, or for a charge, fee or penalty that followed.
Nothing in this clause limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited, including liability for fraud or for our own wilful misconduct.
limitationOfLiability.jurisdictionHeading: Why this clause needs a lawyer more than the other four
limitationOfLiability.jurisdictionNote: This is the most jurisdiction-sensitive clause in these terms, and that is why no number appears in it. Liability caps are not boilerplate in the Philippines: the Civil Code — articles 1170 to 1174 — governs when liability for negligence or bad faith may be limited at all, and the Consumer Act constrains what a supplier may disclaim to a consumer. A limitation clause copied from a United States or European agreement can simply be void here. No cap is stated here, deliberately. What is above is the shape of the clause; the limits inside it are for Philippine counsel to set, or to replace.

changesToTheseTerms.heading: How these terms change, and when a change takes effect
paragraphs: These terms will change. Five clauses are drafts waiting on counsel and two have not been written at all, so change here is not a possibility, it is a certainty. When it happens we say so before it takes effect, not after.

A material change — anything that alters what you are agreeing to, what we disclaim, what a subscription costs or how it renews — is announced on this page and inside the app before it takes effect, and the effective date below is updated in the same release. Corrections that change no obligation, such as a typo or a sentence made clearer, are made without an announcement.
Continuing to use PeraPlano after a change takes effect is how you accept it. If you do not accept it, uninstalling ends the agreement — there is no account to close and nothing to cancel.
Earlier versions of these terms are not archived on this site today. When they are, they will be linked from here.

effectiveDate.heading: Effective date
effectiveDate.label: This version of these terms takes effect on
paragraphs: The date above is rendered from a single constant in this site's source rather than typed into a sentence, so an edit to these terms that forgets to move the date is an edit that cannot happen quietly.

It says when this text became the published text. It does not say the text is finished: this version has not been reviewed by Philippine counsel, five of its clauses are stamped as drafts, and two more have not been drafted at all.

installedApps.title: Which apps you have installed
installedApps.intro: During setup, PeraPlano has to show you the bank and e-wallet apps you actually have, so you can choose whose notifications it should read. Doing that means asking Android which apps are installed on the phone. This page states exactly what that check reads, what it does not, the permission it needs, and the fact that Google may not accept it.

whatIsRead.heading: What is read
paragraphs: PeraPlano reads the package names of the applications installed on your phone — identifier strings such as com.globe.gcash.android. That is the whole of it.
A package name is a label, not a window. It says that an app is present on the phone. It says nothing about what is inside it, and the check asks Android for nothing else.

whatIsNeverRead.heading: What is never read
paragraphs: The check returns a list of names. None of the following is requested, and none of it becomes available to PeraPlano as a result of it:
bullets: Nothing inside any other app: no contents, no screens, no data of any kind.
No usage statistics. PeraPlano does not read how often you open an app or when you last used one, and it does not hold the usage-access permission that would make that possible.
No accessibility service. Using accessibility APIs to collect data is ruled out for this product, and violates Play policy besides.
No SMS permission. Bank SMS reach PeraPlano only as notifications posted by your own messaging app, like any other notification.
No location, no contacts, no call log. None of them has any use in this product.

why.heading: Why it is done at all
paragraphs: Setup asks you which providers PeraPlano should read. For that question to be answerable, the list in front of you has to be the apps you actually have.

Before this check existed, that list was built from thirteen guessed, unverified package names, matched against a listener history that is empty on a fresh install. It asked you to recognise something you had no way to recognise. Reading the installed list replaces a guess with a fact.

It also makes the choice that follows mean something. When the list is one you recognise, ticking nothing is a decision; when it is a list of guesses, ticking nothing usually means the list was unrecognisable.

thePermission.heading: The permission, and what it means at review
paragraphs: Reading the full list of installed apps on current Android versions requires QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, which Google Play classifies as a restricted permission. Declaring it means submitting a declaration form with every release.
What follows is what PeraPlano's own decision record says about that form, published here rather than kept internal.
thePermission.risk: Google's enumerated permitted uses do not obviously cover detecting which bank apps you have installed — the financial carve-out is worded for fraud and security checks. We make the declaration on the basis that the check exists only to configure which notifications you have asked PeraPlano to read. Google may disagree, and a rejection is a live possibility.

theAlternative.heading: If the declaration is refused
paragraphs: App discovery sits behind a single interface with two implementations. One is the check described above. The other is a <queries> manifest allowlist: a fixed list of known Philippine bank and e-wallet package names, declared in the app's manifest, which Android will answer without any restricted permission. If a review ever bounces, the swap is one implementation, not a redesign of setup.

What that would cost you, stated plainly: only apps on the list could be detected. A newly launched e-wallet, or one that has not been added yet, would not appear in your picker until an app update ships with its package name on the list. The check has no such limit, which is why it is the one in use.

whereItGoes.heading: Where the result goes
paragraphs: The result configures the picker you see during setup. What is kept afterwards is your provider selection — the providers you chose — not a copy of your app inventory.

Nothing about it is transmitted. The check runs on the phone, its answer is used on the phone, and no part of it is sent anywhere. The privacy notice describes how everything else PeraPlano holds is stored and for how long.

dataDeletion.title: Delete your data
dataDeletion.intro: Everything PeraPlano records lives in an encrypted database on the phone you installed it on. Deleting it is therefore something you do on the device, and it is final: there is no copy on our servers to restore it from, and nothing held there for us to delete on your behalf. Every deletion route the app has is below, from the smallest to the largest.
dataDeletion.sourceNote: The two retention periods on this page — the 30-day purge of raw notification text, and the 24-month limit on support correspondence — are taken from PeraPlano's internal privacy and compliance document, which is still marked {status} and has not been reviewed by Philippine privacy counsel. They are commitments we intend to keep, not clauses a lawyer has signed off.

deleteOne.heading: Delete a single record
paragraphs: Most of the time the thing you want gone is one transaction — a parse that was wrong, or a payment you would rather not keep. Open it and delete it from its detail screen. Nothing else is affected.

If the record should exist but a field is wrong, change the field instead of destroying the record. Every parsed field — amount, direction, wallet, category, merchant and note — is editable on that same screen, and a correction you make in the Review Queue becomes a rule that applies to what arrives afterwards.

stopWithoutDeleting.heading: Stop the app recording anything, without deleting what it has
paragraphs: Stopping and deleting are different problems, and PeraPlano keeps them apart. These controls live in More → Settings → Privacy, and none of them touches what you have already recorded.
bullets: Pause listening. Reading stops entirely until you turn it back on. The change is visible on Home and in settings, so a paused app never looks like a working one.
Pause one provider. Stop parsing a single provider's notifications while the rest keep working.
Turn off diagnostics. Stops the aggregate telemetry counters described in the privacy notice. Nothing in the app is gated behind leaving it on, and no feature is lost by switching it off.

deleteEverything.heading: Delete everything
deleteEverything.intro: Three routes destroy all of it. They differ mainly in how much they tell you before they act.

routes.detail: The confirmation screen states exactly what will be destroyed, before anything is destroyed.

routes.action: Settings → Apps → PeraPlano → Storage → Clear data.
routes.detail: This destroys the encrypted database and every setting. The app stays installed and returns to its first-run state, as though it had just been downloaded.
Removes the app and its data together.

deleteEverything.recommendation: Use the first. It is the only route that knows what it is deleting, and therefore the only one that can tell you. Clear data and Uninstall are the phone's blunt instruments: they work, and they say nothing about what went with them. All three are irreversible, and an export taken beforehand is the only way back.

selfDeleting.heading: Some of it deletes itself
paragraphs: The raw text of the notifications PeraPlano reads is kept for 30 days and then purged, with or without any action from you. While it is kept it stays on the phone — never in a backup, never in diagnostics, never in a support message.

After the purge, a transaction the app recorded automatically keeps its structured fields, but the screen that answers "why was this recorded?" can no longer show you the notification behind it. It says the original is no longer retained, rather than showing you nothing.

removeFromBetaList.heading: Take me off the beta tester list
paragraphs: The beta signup list is the one thing about you that sits on our side rather than on your phone. It holds the Google account email you gave us, a first name, an optional phone model and the date.
Write to the support address and say you want off the list. The row is deleted. You do not have to prove who you are or give a reason, because the list is not tied to any account.
Leaving the list does not remove you from the closed test itself. Leave that from the test's page in the Play Store, or say so in the same message and the tester entry goes too.

outOfOurReach.heading: What deleting in the app cannot reach
paragraphs: Two things survive a wipe, because neither was ever inside the app's boundary.
bullets: Exports you saved or shared. A CSV export is an ordinary unencrypted file that lives wherever you put it — a downloads folder, a chat thread, a cloud drive. The app warns you of that when it makes one. It is outside the app's protection from that moment, and wiping the app does not touch it; delete those copies yourself.

Support correspondence. Anything you have written to support sits in the support mailbox and is kept no longer than 24 months after the case is closed. Ask for it to be deleted sooner and it will be. This is also why the app asks you not to paste raw notification text into a support message.
outOfOurReach.supportHeading: Ask for support correspondence to be deleted

ifAccountsEverExist.heading: If accounts ever exist
paragraphs: PeraPlano does not offer accounts today. There is no sign-in, no identity held on any server, and so nothing of that kind that could be deleted — which is why this page is a set of instructions for your phone rather than a form.

If a sign-in identity is ever introduced, it would arrive with cloud backup, which our planning documents describe as a future paid feature. Google Play's account-deletion policy would then apply, and a deletion route would appear on this page beside the instructions above: reachable from the web without installing anything, as well as from inside the app.

That route would remove the sign-in identity and all server-side backup data within 30 days. The ledger on the phone would survive unless you asked for that to go as well, and the screen would say so plainly before you chose.
None of it exists yet. Until it does, the instructions above are the only deletion there is to describe, because on-device storage is the only storage there is.

installed-apps.heading: Why this page exists
installed-apps.body: Google Play requires an app that can see which apps are installed to say so in public, in plain language, and to name what it does with the answer. This is that page, and the list below is the whole of it.

data-deletion.heading: Why this page exists
data-deletion.body: Google Play requires a public route to deleting your data, reachable without installing anything. Because PeraPlano keeps your ledger on your phone and nowhere else, most of what follows is something you do on the device rather than something you ask us for.

beta.title: Become a beta tester
beta.tagline: Test it before launch. Keep Plus for life.
beta.lede: We need a small group of people willing to run their real money through PeraPlano and tell us what it gets wrong.

items.title: Plus, free, permanently
items.body: When paid tiers arrive after public release, everyone on this list keeps Plus at no cost. Not a trial, not a discount, not a first year.

items.title: A direct line
items.body: One person builds this. What you report goes to them, not into a queue.

items.title: Your corrections ship
items.body: Every misread notification you flag becomes a parser fix, and it lands before launch rather than after it.

asks.heading: What we are asking of you
asks.lede: Worth being blunt about, because a tester who installs the app and never opens it helps nobody.
items: An Android phone you actually use for money. GCash, Maya, a bank app — whatever already sends you notifications.
A few weeks of using it as your real tracker, rather than as a demo you open once.
Telling us when a notification is read wrong, or missed completely. That is the whole job.

why.heading: Why we need a Google account email
why.body: Google Play closed testing works from an email list. The address you give us goes into Play Console, and Google sends you the invitation and the opt-in link. It has to be the Google account signed in to the Play Store on the phone you will test on, or the invitation reaches nobody.
why.passwordNote: We will never ask for your password. No page on this site has a password field, and no part of PeraPlano ever needs one.

form.heading: Join the beta list
form.emailHint: The account signed in to the Play Store on your test phone.
form.firstNameHint: So the invitation is not addressed to a stranger.
form.deviceHint: Optional. Tells us which devices are actually covered.
form.devicePlaceholder: Samsung A54, Redmi Note 12, Infinix Hot 30
form.consentLabel: I agree to PeraPlano keeping these details in order to invite me to the closed test.
form.successBody: Watch for an invitation from Google Play. You have to tap the opt-in link inside it before the test build becomes installable — nothing happens until you do.
form.duplicateHeading: You were already on the list
form.duplicateBody: Nothing changed, and nothing was duplicated. The invitation still comes from Google Play.

errors.email: Enter the Google account email you use on the Play Store.
errors.consent: Tick the box so we know we may keep your email.
errors.rate: Too many attempts from this connection. Wait a minute, then try again.
errors.server: Something went wrong on our side. Try again in a moment.

form.closedHeading: Signups are not open from this page yet
form.closedBody: The list is not accepting submissions here yet. Write to the support address below and you will be added by hand — it reaches the same list.

data.heading: What we do with it
items: It is used for exactly one thing: adding you to the closed test in Google Play Console.
It is kept in a private spreadsheet, and shared with Google, because Play is how the test is distributed.
It is kept until public release plus ninety days, or until you ask to be removed, whichever comes first.
No ads, no selling, no newsletter. Getting removed takes one message and no explanation.
data.linkLabel: How this sits in the privacy notice

promise.heading: About the Plus promise
promise.body: A promise about money belongs with the other commercial commitments rather than only on a page that is trying to recruit you. The clause on the terms page is the version that binds us, including what happens if the tiers are ever reorganised.
